scope-2002: GOBACK executed in a method (object or factory) acts as EXIT METHOD
GOBACK RAISING (EXCEPTION/identifier/LAST) in a method raises in the invoking element as EXIT METHOD RAISING would
evidence-2002: GOBACK in an object method returns to the INVOKE: covered by probes-t-distant/p01_goback_method.cob (IN-M1/AFTER-M1)

GOBACK RAISING EXCEPTION in an object method: covered by p01 (DECL in the invoker, then AFTER-M2); in a factory method: conformance:cases/14.9.18-GOBACK/pb1177_invoke_self_new_raising (accept [2002], ran clean at --std 2002 this session)

citations.quote: If a GOBACK statement is executed in a method, the method operates as if executing an EXIT METHOD statement
the program operates as if executing a STOP statement

cases.reason: The pointer is the 2023 rule for GOBACK in a program not under a calling element (STOP semantics, RAISING ignored); its witnesses (goback_raising_main, StopGobackExitCodeTests) show the main-program case only. The 2002 rule governs GOBACK in a METHOD, which the pointer's evidence does not reach. Probe p01 at --std 2002: plain GOBACK in a method returns to the INVOKE and the following statement is not reached; GOBACK RAISING EXCEPTION EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW in a method sets the condition in the invoker, whose USE procedure runs and RESUMEs. Output IN-M1/AFTER-M1/IN-M2/DECL/AFTER-M2 matches the rule.
cases.needs: a 2002 witness for GOBACK in a method: p01_goback_method.cob (object method, plain and RAISING) and pb1177_invoke_self_new_raising (factory, accept [2002]) are candidates

or in an output procedure of another MERGE statement
